title: Theorem
summary: A theorem is a statement accompanied by a valid derivation from declared assumptions in a declared system.

content.plain: A theorem is a statement accompanied by a valid derivation from declared assumptions in a declared system.
content.exact: P is a theorem of T relative to proof calculus S when T ⊢ₛ P. The claim is incomplete unless T, S, and the reading of P are recoverable.
content.example: The Pythagorean theorem is a family of precisely stated results whose assumptions depend on the geometry used.
content.caveat: The label theorem records derivational status, not importance or universal truth across all models.
